text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said Thursday its pre-tax profits totalled $881 million pounds ($1.4 billion) in the first quarter, an increase of 1.4 percent from the year-earlier period, despite rising competition.

The British telecommunications giant said pre-tax profits in the three months to June 30 rose to 881 million pounds ($1.4 billion) from 869 million ($1.4 billion) on 4.3 percent higher sales of 3.8 billion pounds ($6.2 billion).

"BT continues to deliver sound results despite having made over 200 million pounds ($327 million) worth of price reductions in the quarter, more than half of which related to international calls," BT Chairman Sir Iain Vallance said in a statement accompanying the results.
"Demand for inland calls is healthy and there is strong growth in our newer services."
Amid rising competition, revenue from domestic telephone calls was flat at 1.23 billion pounds ($2 billion) with volume growth being offset almost entirely by price cuts.
Both domestic and international call volume growth over a 12 month period rose to 8 percent from about 7 percent, BT said.

"The results were ahead of expectations and that had to do with lower costs in some segments," said one analyst. "That's good and in a normal world the stock would be better, but we're not living in a normal world. These numbers are incidental to the bigger picture.
The stock has weakened recently in response to uncertainty over its planned merger with U.S. long distance company MCI Communications.

MCI surprised BT earlier this month -- and sparked calls for the merger to be re-negotiated or even abandoned -- by forecasting losses of $800 million this year and more next year because of delays breaking into local phone service.
